kata.name: Flyweight sharing law F-Closure: a declared instance no key can produce — the kernel emits no finding (null result, gap recorded)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md (Flyweight row, re-opened by naming the law first); fixtures/katas/flyweight/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.8
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered null result: 'every declared flyweight instance is the factory's image' has no kernel predicate. Injectivity holds (distinct intrinsic values) and the handle equation holds, so check is expected to emit nothing while the conventional pool-closure assertion identifies the orphan; the entry is killed with the gap recorded

expected.detail: row 1 is declared with a distinct intrinsic state, so the injectivity key holds; no client handle or key names it, so equation 0 holds; check emits no finding. The conventional pool-closure assertion identifies the orphan. No kernel surface states surjectivity onto the factory's image: a recorded gap, never a fabricated finding

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py --assert, executed before the probe arm: the pool-closure assertion lists every declared flyweight row that is not in the factory's image and names row 1

baseline.artifact: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py sha256:c5c9c28bc4e1bb75a7b2fb64bf41a66d908cd3fee468f7fd00150c26cdbd6d30 (scripted conventional Flyweight test: handle identity, interning pairs, pool closure)

expressibility_gap.invariant: every declared flyweight instance is in the image of the factory (F-Closure)
expressibility_gap.why: declarative keys state injectivity only; equations relate path values from the same source row; check emits no unreachable-row finding. `query --follow factory --direction backward` computes the preimage operationally, but a query result is data, not a finding, so the law has no truth-valued surface

expressibility_gap.invariant: numeric instance counts and share counts (F-Capacity)
expressibility_gap.why: no arithmetic predicate exists over declared row counts; the injectivity key observes colliding pairs, not pool size or share counts

discrepancies: a conventional pool-closure assertion names the orphan while the probe is silent; both arms are recorded and the unique set is empty (probe elements minus baseline elements), so this is a null result with the gap named, never parity-as-victory

the gap is precise: the missing surface is a surjectivity/image-closure predicate over declared rows. `query` can compute the same fact but returns a closure, not a verdict, so it is a probe rather than a law
procedure: 1. The law was named before the fixtures (README 'Law named first'): F-Intern (declarative key on the intrinsic tuple), F-Handle (path equation key x factory = flyweight), plus the two laws named as unexpressible (F-Closure, F-Capacity). The fault set and its expectations were pinned in fixtures/katas/flyweight/faults.json.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/flyweight_baseline.py, sha256 pinned in comparison.baseline) was executed first: the complete conventional Flyweight contract (handle identity per client, interning pairs over declared rows, pool closure), never calling catherine.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, findings recorded verbatim; no kernel change and no new CLI.

4. Witnesses were mapped to the pre-registered element vocabulary: an equation witness {equation, row} to flyweight:handle-identity@Client#<row>; a key witness {key, rows:[lo,hi]} to flyweight:interning-pair@Flyweight#<lo>/Flyweight#<hi>; baseline-only pool-closure elements carry no probe counterpart. unique = probe elements minus baseline elements.

5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived. Expressibility is recorded separately in expressibility_gap and never inflates the verdict.
